about: PROVISIONAL REALIZATIONS: his provisional realization choices for one Learning Goal's activity, held as contract-shaped contributions so the engine builds them exactly as it builds any other knowledge, while every item stays marked as his choice for that activity and never as canonical knowledge. Added 15 October 2026 (stage K2) for his reply filed 17 October 2026: 'The priority remains producing one complete, representative Play Out from the Back activity through the normal generation pathway, without introducing unnecessary architecture or treating this first realization as the canonical version of the Learning Goal.' and, of the post-regain area, 'I also agree that the post-regain area is a provisional realization choice, not canonical Goalkeeper Build-Out knowledge.' HOW IT IS READ (back/src/system/derivation/corpus.ts, loadProvisionalRealizations): a realization joins a derivation ONLY where the selected goal's authorization record names it (learning-goal-authorizations.json, provisionalRealization); nothing selects it otherwise, and no goal is named in code. It is never written into contracts.json, never keyed to the context it realizes, and never applied as a restatement. Its shape is the Sport Profile's precedent (SD-17: a source outside the representation enters as items under its own contract), with three differences the loader enforces and refuses the whole file on: every item has basis OWNER_RULING, quotes him (words, citedAs) and carries category PROVISIONAL_REALIZATION_CHOICE, which reaches every support entry and the rendering fixture; a realization holds NO declaration (a provisional choice says what this activity does, never what knowledge does not constrain, so no qualified or unqualified non-claim can enter through this file, and his M6 disjointness proof is never needed here); and an item may not name a designation refused below. realizationChoices names the realization-choices file whose entries REPLACE the game form's for the lines they list, each replacement declared (supplied-realization.ts). notWithPracticeSituations lists the practice situations the realization was not designed for: that combination is refused, not built.

refusedDesignations.words: Please use the assigned team roles rather than referring generically to "the defending team," since possession and defensive responsibilities change during play.
refusedDesignations.note: Our application of his D7 sentence to the realization's own facts: a fact about the building or pressing team is written by the role the team holds, never by a possession-relative or episode designation (ATTACKING_TEAM, DEFENDING_TEAM), by the team whose build-out episode it is (BUILD_OUT_TEAM, which a regain episode never is), or by the team scored against (CONCEDING_TEAM: when a new build-out episode begins, 'The designated building team restarts', his D5). The list is ours, put to him in our email of 17 October; it narrows what this file may say and widens nothing.

words: The priority remains producing one complete, representative Play Out from the Back activity through the normal generation pathway, without introducing unnecessary architecture or treating this first realization as the canonical version of the Learning Goal.
This is a provisional realization choice, not a general rule that all build-out activities must stop when progression is achieved.
This is the initial activity configuration, not a universal requirement for Play Out from the Back.

notWithPracticeSituations.because: His decisions of 17 October describe a build-out begun by the building team's goalkeeper or a controlled defensive restart, at a location the coach chooses; the From Goal Kicks practice situation brings its own formal restart, which he keeps apart: 'Please preserve the distinction between a controlled defensive restart and a formal goal kick. If the coach selects a formal goal kick, the applicable Laws of the Game should govern it. The three facts you've identified can be recorded, but they should be treated as part of that specific restart type, not imposed on all build-out starts.' (Christian, 15 October 2026, item 4 - his first reply of that day). That this first activity does not cover the situation is our reading, put to him in our email of 17 October: 'This provisional activity does not cover the From Goal Kicks practice situation. That combination is refused for now.'

realizations.note: EMPTY AT LANDING, 15 October 2026 (stage K2): the carrier, its loader, its gate on the record and its replacement realization choices land before the choices themselves. The items his 17 October decisions authorize (the role blocks, the allocation by role, the start and restart transitions, the starting relationship and the targets keyed by role) join in later stages, each when the engine can carry it, so that no item enters a game the engine would misread. Measured at landing: with this realization empty every Learning Goal, every demonstration and the A04 fixture derive byte-identically. FIRST ITEMS, 15 October 2026 (stage K3): the role blocks of his D2(a) and M1 - the two roles (A01-R1-B1-1, A01-R1-B1-2) and how they pass between the teams (A01-R1-B3-1, the coach calls the next block, the exchange vocabulary's one member). The engine now derives a game holding them as two complete games, one per role block, and checks the two against each other (RB-1 to RB-8). They change no production outcome: the authorization record's gap entries still refuse A01 at 'knowledge', before derivation; behind those entries (a TEST-ONLY copy) each block stops where the single game stopped, at GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE. ALLOCATION AND REASSIGNMENT, 15 October 2026 (stage K4): his D6 starting configurations by role (A01-R1-P2-1, A01-R1-P2-2, each citing the relationship RPC-001~EM-0006 he confirmed on 18 October, under which the possession game's equal-numbers item defers, ruling C56), one goalkeeper for the building role (A01-R1-P3-1), and his 18 October answer to RD-1 as a reassignment kept apart from the role exchange (A01-R1-B4-1/B7-1 the goalkeeper, A01-R1-B4-2/B7-2 one outfield player, register version 11), with his testing boundaries held as data (testingBoundaries). Measured on the possession game with this realization (no context): 12 players give 6 + goalkeeper against 5 in both blocks, every cross-block check passing; 13 and 10 are refused as not decided; 11 is refused at the membership check (testingBoundaries.note). The record's three allocation entries are carried; A01 is refused at 'knowledge' on six entries (was eight), and behind them still at GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE. STARTS AND RESTARTS, 15 October 2026 (stage K5): his D1(a), D5, D7, M3 and M4 of 17 October and his 18 October answer to RD-2 as transitions - the start, the after-score restart and the coach-judged conclusion (A01-R1-T1-1..3), each stopping and restarting play, awarded to the team holding the building role and taken by its goalkeeper from the feet at a location the coach chooses (A01-R1-T6-1, T7-1, T2-1, T3-1, T4-1, T5-1); and four ordinary out-of-play restarts partitioned by who touched the ball last (A01-R1-T1-4..7, T1b-1, T1c-1, T6-2, T7-2, T7-3, T3-2..3, T4-2..3, T5-2..3) - a throw-in where the ball crossed a touchline, the coach's method and place on an end line, the episode continuing off the pressing team and the build-out ending off the building team. Register version 12 carries the capabilities (the coach-judged trigger, FROM_THE_FEET, the coach's restart location and method, the opening holder of possession entailed by the start's awardee), and ruling C58 types the build-out begin condition in his acknowledged wording, so GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE passes in both blocks with one awardee. Measured: the record's three restart entries are carried; A01 is refused at 'knowledge' on three entries, and behind them each block stops on the progression reference (RPC-001-18.d, open text, stage K6). That the end-line place is the coach's too, and that any player of the awarded team takes an end-line restart, are our readings of his item 2, put to him for a one-line confirmation. CREDIT BOUND, 17 October 2026 (stage M1): his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 1 and item 3 C, as row B8 (register version 14) on the two roles - the building team's credit confined to the build-out episode (A01-R1-B8-1) and the pressing team's stated as the whole game (A01-R1-B8-2) - with A01-R1-T7-3 now citing his 3 C confirmation. GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE's fourth and fifth clauses decide it in both blocks. ALSO COUNTS, 17 October 2026 (stage M2): his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 2, as row V27 (register version 14) for the pressing role only - a controlled regain inside the target it attacks counts as the one primary event and earns its value (A01-R1-V27-1; trigger A01-R1-V29-1, control A01-R1-V30-1, exclusion A01-R1-V31-1, in his words). GA-ONE-PRIMARY-EVENT's added clauses decide it in both blocks, and it is said only in approved words, so until he approves a sentence the activity is refused at communication naming its four fields.

items.choice: The first activity is played in blocks, and in each block one team is the building team.
items.words: Approve D2(a): Coach-controlled blocks. One team builds out while the other presses. The coach determines when the teams exchange roles.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, D2: "Approve D2(a): Coach-controlled blocks. One team builds out while the other presses." and "This is the initial activity configuration, not a universal requirement for Play Out from the Back." M1: "M1 — Role exchange by block: Approved. Keep role assignments separate from fixed ends." D7: "The building team attempts controlled progression into its designated target."
items.fitNote: Establishes the building role as an element of activityRoles[] (register version 10, row B1). Which team holds it in a block is not stated here and cannot be: the two blocks are the two bindings of the two roles to the two end-assigned teams, derived one game each. The token BUILDING is ours, named from his D7 wording.

items.choice: In each block the other team is the pressing team.
items.words: One team builds out while the other presses.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, D2: "One team builds out while the other presses." D7: "The pressing team attempts to prevent progression, regain possession, and reach its post-regain target." and "Please use the assigned team roles rather than referring generically to "the defending team," since possession and defensive responsibilities change during play."
items.fitNote: Establishes the pressing role as an element of activityRoles[] (row B1). A role, never a possession-relative designation: the team holding it keeps it for the block whoever has the ball. The token PRESSING is ours, named from his D7 wording.

items.choice: The roles pass between the teams when the coach calls the next block; there is no block duration.
items.words: Roles exchange when the coach calls for the next block.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, D7: "Roles exchange when the coach calls for the next block." D2: "The coach determines when the teams exchange roles. No mandatory block duration is needed." M1: "The coach controls the exchange. No new block-duration system is needed."
items.fitNote: Every role passes by the coach's call (row B3, closed list B3.exchange with one member). No duration, count, timer, trigger or window is stated, and none can be: the list holds nothing else.

items.choice: The activity starts with five outfield players in the team holding the pressing role, in both starting configurations he named.
items.words: For the initial 12-player demonstration, I favor six outfield players plus one goalkeeper building out against five pressing players. This uses all 12 players and creates a modest numerical advantage for the building team. However, five outfield players plus a goalkeeper against five pressing players is also a legitimate configuration when the roster supports it.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, D6: "For the initial 12-player demonstration, I favor six outfield players plus one goalkeeper building out against five pressing players." "However, five outfield players plus a goalkeeper against five pressing players is also a legitimate configuration when the roster supports it." "Please authorize this initial numerical asymmetry through the appropriate existing knowledge relationship, rather than hardcoding it to Play Out from the Back." The relationship, confirmed in his reply filed 18 October 2026, item 5: "Goalkeeper Build-Out with Participant Composition."
items.fitNote: The STARTING count of the team holding the pressing role in a block (ROLE_HOLDER_PRESSING, block-scoped), not a rule of every session: his two adjustments ('Add a pressing player' among them) depart from it during a session and are recorded as such in the authorization record (authorizedAdjustments), never as values here. Five in both configurations he named. Cites RPC-001~EM-0006, under which the possession game's equal-numbers item GF2-14.b defers (ruling C56).

items.choice: The team holding the building role starts with six outfield players, or five where the roster supports his alternative configuration; the session's player count decides which.
items.words: For the initial 12-player demonstration, I favor six outfield players plus one goalkeeper building out against five pressing players. This uses all 12 players and creates a modest numerical advantage for the building team. However, five outfield players plus a goalkeeper against five pressing players is also a legitimate configuration when the roster supports it.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, D6: "For the initial 12-player demonstration, I favor six outfield players plus one goalkeeper building out against five pressing players." items.fitNote: The two members are his two configurations, six and five; the typed bound states them and no other number. The roster closes it from the session total and refuses rather than choose: with one goalkeeper and five pressing players, only six fits 12 players and only five fits 11, and any other count fits neither and is refused with a sentence that the configuration has not been decided for it - his 'acceptable current testing boundaries' (18 October, item 7), held as data here and in testingBoundaries below, never as a limit in code. Cites RPC-001~EM-0006 (ruling C56).

items.choice: One active goalkeeper, for the team holding the building role in each block.
items.words: For this first asymmetrical activity, I favor one active goalkeeper serving the team currently building out.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, D6: "For this first asymmetrical activity, I favor one active goalkeeper serving the team currently building out." "When teams exchange building and pressing roles, the active goalkeeper should support the newly designated building team. The goalkeeper does not need to remain permanently assigned to one team or end." "Please do not assign a goalkeeper an inactive role solely to preserve a symmetrical team structure."
items.fitNote: Keyed to the role, so the count is the building role's in every block; the pressing role's team has none because nothing here reaches it and the possession game does not constrain goalkeepers (GF2 P3 NON_CLAIMED), not because a zero is written. A second available goalkeeper is not idled: the roster counts a performer available and not involved among the outfield players. Who the goalkeeper is with after an exchange is the recorded reassignment below (A01-R1-B4-1), not this item: a role exchange moves no player by itself.

items.choice: At each exchange of roles the goalkeeper moves to the team that becomes the building team.
items.words: When the teams exchange building and pressing roles, the goalkeeper and one outfield player transfer to the newly designated building team. This preserves the 6 + GK versus 5 relationship in both blocks.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 18 October 2026, item 1: "Approve Option 1(a) for the initial prototype." "When the teams exchange building and pressing roles, the goalkeeper and one outfield player transfer to the newly designated building team. This preserves the 6 + GK versus 5 relationship in both blocks." "I confirm that the previously approved fixed team ends do not prohibit participant reassignment." "One architectural distinction: role exchange and participant reassignment should remain separate capabilities. Exchanging roles should not inherently require players to change teams. This particular realization uses both mechanisms to preserve its intended numerical relationship."
items.fitNote: A reassignment (register version 11, row B4), the capability he asked to be kept apart from the role exchange: the performers counted by P3 (the specialized role) move to the team newly holding the building role. Its count is A01-R1-B7-1. His Option 1(c), keeping membership and changing the numerical problem, stays expressible: a realization that records no reassignment keeps every team's performers in every block (cross-block check RB-M).

items.choice: One goalkeeper moves at each exchange.
items.words: When the teams exchange building and pressing roles, the goalkeeper and one outfield player transfer to the newly designated building team.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 18 October 2026, item 1: "When the teams exchange building and pressing roles, the goalkeeper and one outfield player transfer to the newly designated building team."
items.fitNote: 'the goalkeeper': one, the active goalkeeper of his D6 ('one active goalkeeper serving the team currently building out').

items.choice: At each exchange of roles the outfield players that keep each role's outfield count move to the team that becomes the building team: one at 12 players; at 11 players none, and then no reassignment of outfield players is established.
items.words: When the teams exchange building and pressing roles, the goalkeeper and one outfield player transfer to the newly designated building team. This preserves the 6 + GK versus 5 relationship in both blocks.

items.fitNote: A reassignment of the performers counted by P2 (outfield players) to the team newly holding the building role. Its count is A01-R1-B7-2. Which player moves is not stated and is not a property of the game. Since 17 October 2026 (stage M4) that count is relative, so at 11 players, where it resolves to 0, this element is not established in the game (derivation/reassignment.ts resolveRelativeCounts); his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 3 F, confirms that case.

items.choice: As many outfield players move at each exchange as keep the building team's outfield count: one at 12 players, none at 11.
items.words: This preserves the 6 + GK versus 5 relationship in both blocks. … With 5 outfield players plus a goalkeeper against 5 outfield players, only the goalkeeper changes teams at a role exchange. No additional outfield player transfer is required.
items.citedAs: his reply filed 18 October 2026, item 1; his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 3 F
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 18 October 2026, item 1: "the goalkeeper and one outfield player transfer to the newly designated building team." "This preserves the 6 + GK versus 5 relationship in both blocks." Reply filed 19 October 2026, item 3 F: "Yes. With 5 outfield players plus a goalkeeper against 5 outfield players, only the goalkeeper changes teams at a role exchange. No additional outfield player transfer is required." "These are approved for the current activity configuration." Until 17 October 2026 (stage M4) the value was 1, his 18 October 'one outfield player', which at 11 players moved an outfield player that configuration does not need, so 11 players was refused at the membership check.
items.fitNote: OUR READING of his stated reason as a relative count, labelled so: register B7 version 2 ({keepsCountOf: R}) - the number of outfield players that keeps, in the block an exchange begins, the outfield count the team holding the building role had before. Read from one block's own game (derivation/reassignment.ts resolveRelativeCounts): at 12 players 6 - 5 = 1, his 'one outfield player'; at 11 players 5 - 5 = 0, so no reassignment of outfield players is established and only the goalkeeper moves (A01-R1-B7-1), his 3 F. The cross-block membership check (RB-M) still compares the second block, built independently, with what the count states.

items.choice: The activity starts with the building team beginning a build-out episode.
items.words: When a new build-out episode begins: … The designated building team restarts.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, D5: "When a new build-out episode begins:" "The designated building team restarts." D7: "Only the building team initiates new build-out episodes." M3: "M3 — Starts and restarts built from knowledge: Approved." "Support goalkeeper or controlled defensive starts, coach-selected restart locations, and activity-specific restart methods." "These choices must remain distinguishable from universal requirements."
items.fitNote: Establishes the start transition element (row T1). The possession game and the context leave the start unauthored (GF2 T3-T5 NOT_AUTHORED "start procedure"; GF2 T1 UNDECLARED "Existence of other transitions never examined"), and nothing formed a start element in any game (measured 15 October 2026). This item answers that for this activity only; nothing canonical changes, and every other game is untouched.

items.choice: A score concludes the episode, and the activity restarts.
items.words: When the building team achieves controlled progression into its designated target, the successful build-out counts and the episode concludes. The activity then restarts to create another opportunity to solve the build-out problem.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, D1: "Approve D1(a) for the first activity." "When the building team achieves controlled progression into its designated target, the successful build-out counts and the episode concludes." "The activity then restarts to create another opportunity to solve the build-out problem." "This is a provisional realization choice, not a general rule that all build-out activities must stop when progression is achieved." D5: "An episode concludes when either team scores or when the coach judges that the meaningful attacking opportunity has ended."
items.fitNote: Establishes the after-score transition element (row T1), one for both teams: after either team scores the activity restarts with the building team (D5), so no split by which target was scored is needed. Goalkeeper Build-Out's own non-authorship stays canonical and unchanged (RPC-001 T6 SCORE NOT_AUTHORED, its notAuthored 4: "Whether play stops at the moment of the scoring event"), so continued play after progression remains open for every other realization, as he said.

items.choice: The coach may judge that the episode has concluded, during play or at a stoppage, and the activity restarts.
items.words: An episode concludes when either team scores or when the coach judges that the meaningful attacking opportunity has ended. The coach may make that judgment at a stoppage or during play.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 17 October 2026, D5: "An episode concludes when either team scores or when the coach judges that the meaningful attacking opportunity has ended." "The coach may make that judgment at a stoppage or during play." M4: "M4 — Coach-judged episode conclusion: Approved." "Support one explicit coach-judged event representing the conclusion of a meaningful episode." "Do not substitute a timer, possession change, or arbitrary pass count." reply filed 18 October 2026, item 2: "At any stoppage, the coach may instead conclude the current episode and initiate another build-out."
items.fitNote: Establishes the coach-judged conclusion transition element (row T1) on the trigger registered for his M4 (register version 12, trigger version 4, with its semantics). Reachable because the game holds a start element (the trigger's structural prerequisite, our operational proposal). No timer, possession change or pass count stands in for it.

items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 19 October 2026, item 1: "The important distinction is that the building team's scoring opportunity applies only during an active build-out episode." "If the building team loses possession, that scoring opportunity ends. If it subsequently regains possession, play may continue, but the original build-out scoring opportunity is not restored. A deliberate goalkeeper restart is required to initiate another opportunity to earn a build-out point." "This is intentional. Although counterpressing, regaining possession, and exploiting attacking transitions are meaningful parts of the game, they are not the primary Learning Goal for this activity." "Please ensure the underlying scoring eligibility reflects this distinction, rather than relying solely on the coach-facing wording." Item 3 C: "Yes. The build-out scoring episode ends. Ordinary play may continue following the restart, but build-out scoring eligibility does not return until a new deliberate goalkeeper restart." Item 3: "These are approved for the current activity configuration." CONSISTENT existing knowledge, cited as consistent and not as the authority: RPC-001-11.b (with KR-02 and KR-03) places the build-out objective within the build-out episode, and SD-36 scopes the build-out conditions to that episode ("It does NOT automatically extend to subsequent attacking episodes."); none of them says that the build-out team scores only there, so the bound rests on his item 1 and item 3 C.
items.fitNote: OUR GLOSS, labelled so: row B8 (register version 14) on the building role's element - its holder earns the primary event's credit only inside a BUILD_OUT_EPISODE, begun by the transitions the typed begin condition picks out (ruling C58: the start, the restart after a score and the coach-judged conclusion, A01-R1-T1-1..3, taken by its goalkeeper and awarded to it) and ended by every transition that begins another episode (the change of possession, GF2-07.a; the restarts after it plays the ball out, A01-R1-T1-5 and T1-7, which A01-R1-T7-3 makes begin one). GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE's fourth clause checks the first half and its fifth the second, so a reversal of either is refused at structure. A provisional choice for this activity, not Goalkeeper Build-Out knowledge: nothing is written into RPC-001, GF2 or the restatements, and his D1(b) continued-play alternative stays open for any other realization. Said to the coach only in approved words (render-concrete-game.ts WORDED_ONLY).

Stated explicitly rather than left silent, on his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 8: "However, the engine must distinguish between:" "A field explicitly defined as not applicable or requiring no further value." items.fitNote: OUR GLOSS, labelled so: row B8 on the pressing role's element, WHOLE_GAME - its holder's credit is not confined to any episode, which is what his item 2 keeps ('retains its separate objective'). Written explicitly so the pressing role's bound is a stated value, not a silence read as one. An unbounded value states no condition, so it is not withheld from the coach as awaiting approved wording.

items.choice: For the pressing team only, winning the ball inside the target area it attacks also counts as a score, of the same value as any other, when it genuinely establishes possession there; a contested touch, deflection or loose ball does not.
items.words: For the previously flagged corner case, I favor allowing a controlled regain inside that area to count as a score, provided the pressing team genuinely establishes possession.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 19 October 2026, item 2: "The pressing team retains its separate objective of regaining possession and attacking the 5 m target area." "For the previously flagged corner case, I favor allowing a controlled regain inside that area to count as a score, provided the pressing team genuinely establishes possession." "A contested touch, deflection, or loose ball should not qualify." "This gives the pressing team a meaningful incentive to recognize and exploit high-regain opportunities without requiring an arbitrary additional pass or dribble." "This is a provisional scoring choice for the current realization, not a universal rule equating every regain with successful progression." GOVERNANCE: the context's own scoring event is the zone entry, and RPC-001 does not approve a regain as a scoring event (the design verifier read it approved only for other contexts), so this credit rests solely on his explicit item 2, under his answer 9 of 15 October 2026: "Specific knowledge governs where it explicitly defines or specializes a condition." His 17 October D7 still governs what an ENTRY is, and is not changed: "A successful regain alone should not count as controlled progression into the target area." No bonus: the score earns the primary event's own value, as his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 3, asks: "However, please do not automatically add a high-regain bonus."
items.fitNote: OUR GLOSS, labelled so: row V27 (register version 14), one element for the team holding the pressing role in the block (V28, carried from the selector; it resolves to that team per block). Reading 'count as a score' as counting as the one primary event and earning its value (V2), never a second primary event or a value of its own, is OUR READING (SD-113). It is not a new meaning of the zone entry (the vocabulary gloss of target_zone_entered and the V1 'regain' gloss are unchanged), and nothing is written for the building role. Where it counts is the target the pressing team attacks, read through its own team (the register's targetOf), never a written referent. GA-ONE-PRIMARY-EVENT checks it in both blocks: one team, an in-play trigger the game holds and the score that follows, inside its own team's one target, control stated, one element per team, its trigger beginning an episode and none a condition of the primary event is authored for, and no whole-game condition beside it; the context-scoring guard requires every item behind it to be his ruling. A provisional choice for this activity, not Goalkeeper Build-Out knowledge: nothing is written into RPC-001, GF2 or the restatements. Said to the coach only in approved words (render-concrete-game.ts WORDED_ONLY); until he approves a sentence the activity is refused at communication naming its four fields.

items.words: For the previously flagged corner case, I favor allowing a controlled regain inside that area to count as a score, provided the pressing team genuinely establishes possession.
items.basisEvidence: Christian, reply filed 19 October 2026, item 2: "For the previously flagged corner case, I favor allowing a controlled regain inside that area to count as a score, provided the pressing team genuinely establishes possession." Item 3 A: "Yes. The coach determines both, with the understanding that ordinary restarts should preserve meaningful game relationships rather than create an automatic scoring shortcut."
items.fitNote: OUR READING, labelled so: his 'regain' read as the in-play change of possession (POSSESSION_CHANGE, the one member of the closed list V29.trigger), never a restart awarded out of play (OUT_TOUCHLINE, OUT_END_LINE), so an ordinary restart awarded to the pressing team inside or beside its target never scores through this element - our reading of his item 3 A safeguard, not his ruling. The change of possession begins an episode (RPC-001-17.a, T7 true), so the occurrence is evaluated in the episode it begins, and the building team's BUILD_OUT_EPISODE conditions never govern it (OUR INFERENCE from his item 1 and RPC-001-17.a; GA-ONE-PRIMARY-EVENT's episode clause pins it). It is a score, so the restart after a score governs play at that moment.

testingBoundaries.words: The 11–12-player support and 40 × 30 m prototype values are acceptable current testing boundaries, but they should not become permanent architectural limitations.
testingBoundaries.note: DATA, never a limit in code (his item 7). The player counts this realization's own items admit: with one goalkeeper and five pressing players, the building count of five or six (A01-R1-P2-2) fits only 11 and 12 players. The roster finds that from the items alone; this list records what it should find, and a test holds the two together, so a change to either is seen. MEASURED 15 October 2026 (stage K4): at 11 players the teams are 5 + goalkeeper against 5 in both blocks, so only the goalkeeper changes team at the exchange, while his 1(a) moves an outfield player too ('This preserves the 6 + GK versus 5 relationship in both blocks.'); the cross-block membership check refuses it, and the coach is told who changes team has not been decided for 11 players. Which reassignment his alternative configuration takes is his to say. ANSWERED 17 October 2026 (stage M4): his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 3 F, "With 5 outfield players plus a goalkeeper against 5 outfield players, only the goalkeeper changes teams at a role exchange. No additional outfield player transfer is required." A01-R1-B7-2's count is now relative (register B7 version 2), so at 11 players no outfield player moves, only the goalkeeper, and the membership check passes. The 40 x 30 m area joined this record on 15 October 2026 (stage K6) with the starting placements that need it: his values (reply filed 18 October 2026, item 3, "I approve the following provisional values:") are in metres for that area - "The pressure reference should be adjustable in either direction. Twenty meters is our initial hypothesis, not a canonical distance or a requirement for other field sizes." - so they are held for 40 x 30 m only (areas: length 40 m, width 30 m, as recorded), and any other area is refused before derivation with the sentence that the starting positions have not been decided for it. A list in data, never a limit in code.
